content_units: Best Fit for a 5-Year Dublin Commute

For   18,000 km/year  , your total use will be about   90,000 km over 5 years  , so each car would likely end up around   168,000-185,000 km  . With your priorities, the safest choice is the one with the   lowest mechanical risk, strongest service record, and simplest long-term ownership profile  .
Recommended pick: 2018 Toyota Corolla 1.33 petrol
Why it stands out:
- Toyota has the strongest reputation here for   durability and low surprise repair risk
-   Full service history   matters a lot when buying near 90,000 km
- Naturally aspirated   1.33 petrol   is generally lower-risk long term than small turbo petrol alternatives
- Price is near your cap, but still within budget and justified by lower ownership risk
Ownership Risk Comparison
Car   Price   Odometer   Service History   5-Year Risk   Main Risk Notes   Verdict
2018 Toyota Corolla 1.33 petrol   EUR 13,800   92,000 km   Full     Low     Slower engine, but simple and proven; likely lowest major-failure risk     Best overall

2019 Ford Focus 1.0 EcoBoost petrol   EUR 12,900   78,000 km   Partial     Medium-High     Incomplete history is a concern; 1.0 turbo adds more long-term risk sensitivity   Skip unless history is verified
2017 Hyundai i30 1.4 petrol   EUR 12,600   88,000 km   Full     Low-Medium     Good reliability profile; slightly less proven resale/long-term confidence than Toyota   Best value alternative

2018 Volkswagen Golf 1.0 TSI petrol   EUR 13,950   95,000 km   Full     Medium     Good car, but 1.0 TSI complexity and potentially higher repair costs raise 5-year risk   Good, but not for reliability-first
Ranked Recommendation
Option 1: 2018 Toyota Corolla 1.33 petrol   Lowest expected ownership risk over 5 years   Reliability-first winner
- Best match for your stated priority:   dependability over features
- Full history plus Toyota reliability makes it the safest high-mileage keeper
- Likely easiest to own with fewer unexpected bills
Option 2: 2017 Hyundai i30 1.4 petrol   Strong value with sensible long-term risk   Budget-friendly backup
- Cheapest option here with full history
- Simple petrol setup is attractive for steady commuting
- Best fallback if the Corolla fails inspection or negotiation
Option 3: 2018 Volkswagen Golf 1.0 TSI petrol   More polished car, but higher ownership complexity   Trade-off choice
- Fine if you value cabin feel and driving refinement
- Not the best fit for a buyer prioritizing low-risk 5-year ownership
Option 4: 2019 Ford Focus 1.0 EcoBoost petrol   Tempting price/km combo, but history weakens confidence   Highest caution flag
- Partial service history is the biggest red flag in this shortlist
- Cheapest repairs are the ones you avoid by buying the right history
5-Year Ownership Judgment
For your use case, I would optimize in this order:
-   Mechanical simplicity
-   Full documented maintenance
-   Brand reliability at higher mileage
-   Reasonable purchase price
That makes the final call:
Buy the Toyota Corolla   if inspection is clean.
If the Toyota is unavailable or overpriced after inspection,   buy the Hyundai i30  .
Buying Checks Before You Commit
- Confirm   stamped or invoice-backed full service history
- Check if   spark plugs, brake fluid, coolant, and gearbox oil   were ever done if applicable
- Inspect for   clutch wear, suspension knocks, uneven tire wear, and corrosion underneath
- Verify   NCT history  , mileage consistency, and any write-off record
- Get an   independent pre-purchase inspection   before paying
Context for This Recommendation
This comparison assumes:
- You want the   lowest chance of expensive surprises  , not the most fun or best-equipped car
- You will keep the car to roughly   170,000-185,000 km total
- All four cars are otherwise clean-title Irish-market cars with no accident or finance issues
